label: Say the number out loud
note: the book's thesis — three women say their numbers at one table; the cure for solitary rescue
hours-for-dollars — the only lever Keisha grew up watching anyone pull
equity — a share of a thing, not a wage; the $30 for 30% and the Deere certificate
$400 a year for sixteen years becomes the answer Keisha just handled unread
the counterfeit fourth physics — must read as a trap, never a lesson

label: Read before you sign
note: Keisha's planted superpower — steel-bridge rules teach her to read boring documents; the vending ordinance rehearses the annuity contract

label: Never risk money you can't lose

note: the one money rule Denise ever explicitly taught; the $60 borrow breaks it, the coda repays it

label: Small confessions are survivable

note: city hall says yes because she asked precisely; Denise asks one concrete question out loud

label: Isolation is what predators target — disclosure is armor
note: Gary built the pitch for a woman alone; three women and a marked-up contract defeat him

label: Slow and boring survives
note: the certificate old enough to be furniture survived because it was slow
